evidence.quote: The 70-mile long byway takes about 4 hours to drive and provides a memorable journey offering access to several resort towns, recreation areas, popular lakes, and impressive views.

evidence.claim: Highway 168 passes through Prather, rejoins Tollhouse Road north of Tollhouse, then takes the name Huntington Lake Road in Ockenden.

evidence.claim: When the flume and mill began operating in 1894, lumber workers built homes nearby, followed by services, churches and schools.
evidence.quote: The completion in 1894 of the lumber flume and commencement of mill operations provided the impetus for further development of the area around the Clovis Station. The town began to take shape as lumber yard employees built homes close to their employment. Service businesses, churches, and schools became necessary

The Forest Service describes a 70-mile byway to Kaiser Pass Meadow; the highway article identifies the designated segment as Clovis to Huntington Lake. The overview distinguishes the full scenic drive from numbered Highway 168.

Clovis and Shaver Lake town articles give conflicting flume lengths (42 and 65 miles); length omitted. The town article also gives 1919 enlargement and Thomas A. Edison Company, while the lake article gives Southern California Edison purchase in 1917 and dam completion in 1927. Lake article used for those dates; unresolved discrepancy retained here.
